summary: Fumio Enomoto is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a research assistant at Kyoto University (~1980–1985) and as a professor at Osaka University (~1999–2018).

Fumio Masutani was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at the Fifth Higher School and the University of Tokyo. He held professorships at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and Taisho University, and served as president of Tsuru University (1969–1971).

Fumio Matsuda works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He held a post at Komazawa University and served as an executive committee chairman for the Association for the Study of Indian Religions in 1997.

Fumio Ouchi is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. After earning his doctorate at Otani University, he served there as an assistant professor (~1993–2002) and professor (~2002–2013).

Fumio Shoji is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1998–2007). He later served at Rissho University as an assistant professor of Buddhist studies (~2013–2018) and associate professor (~2018).
Fumio Tamamuro is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Meiji University (~1954–1963) and subsequently held an academic post there (~1978–2006).

Futoshi Omae is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He was a lecturer at Kyushu University (attested 1990–1991) and held posts at Shimane Prefectural Junior College of Nursing (attested 1997) and Shimane International Junior College (attested 1998).
Futoshi Takehashi studied Buddhist studies at Otani University (doctoral course attested 1992). He held an assistant post at the Shinshu Otani-ha Research Institute from 1995 to 1997.
Fuyuan Luo is a researcher in Tibetology and religious studies who pursued PhD studies at the University of Cambridge under Adam Yuet Chau (attested 2026).

Fyodor Buslaev was a scholar of linguistics and history/archaeology. He studied at the Faculty of History and Philology of Moscow University (~1834–1838) and took a post at Moscow State University in 1846.

Fyodor Shcherbatskoy was an Indologist and philosopher who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and under Ivan Minaev, Sergey Oldenburg, Georg Bühler, and Hermann Jacobi. He served as professor at Saint Petersburg State University (~1909–1941) and founded the Buddhist Cultural Institute.

Félix Nève was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at KU Leuven and studied under Christian Lassen, Friedrich Wilhelm Thiersch, and Eugène Burnouf. He was a professor at KU Leuven from 1841 until becoming professor emeritus in 1877.

G. B. Palsule was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as a sub-editor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1957) and held a post at Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1987).
G. K. Jenkins was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Bloxham School (~1932–1937) and served at the British Museum from 1947 to 1978.

G. P. Malalasekera was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of London and SOAS under Caroline Rhys Davids and William Stede. He served as lecturer and faculty dean at the University of Ceylon.
G. Srinivasa Murti was a scholar in Indology who served as Director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1938–1949 and 1971).

G. Thomas Tanselle studied at Yale University. He taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1960–1978), served as vice president of the Guggenheim Memorial Foundation (1978–2006), and was an adjunct professor of English at Columbia University (~1978–2005).
G. V. Aston is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who earned a PhD in philosophy at the University of Canterbury (1986–2004) under the supervision of Paul Harrison.

G. V. Srinivasa Rao worked in Indology and history/archaeology, serving as Senior Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India until 1945 and with the Government Epigraphist for India.

id: P:Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso
summary: Ga Shar Khen Zur Geshé Tamdrin Gyatso was an academic figure who studied under the 14th Dalai Lama and Trijang Rinpoche.
